title: Which number best describes each family's height?
description: Two families' heights are summed up by the mean and the median on the board, and one short member shows when the median fits better. Keeko doubts that the mean is the best number for every family.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median is the middle value of the sorted data; with one value far from the rest it describes the group better than the mean. Watch for children who use the mean every time.

source: Find the mean and the median height of {{NAME_8}}'s family (169
video_script.why: The child can find a mean and now meets a group where one value pulls it away.
video_script.substitution: Sorting the values puts the median in the middle, where one far value cannot drag it.
video_script.wrong_answer: the mean is the best number for every family
video_script.wrong_move: uses the mean for every group, although one short member pulls it below four of the five heights

final_answer.value: {{NAME_8}}: mean 164.33 cm, median 164.5 cm; {{NAME_1}}: mean 160.2 cm, median 170 cm; the median represents the family better
final_answer.spoken: the median represents {{NAME_1}}'s family better, with a median of one hundred and seventy centimetres against a mean of one hundred and sixty point two

names.{{NAME_1}}: family whose heights include one short member

maths_rules: median: the middle value of the sorted data; with an even count, halfway between the two middle values
4 of {{NAME_1}}'s 5 family members are taller than 160.2
video_script.design: One idea: the middle of the sorted data. Two rows of height bars stay in the anchor; each row sorts on the stage and its middle lights up.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; two rows of height bars in centimetres, one row of six bars and one row of five bars, one bar much shorter than the rest

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the two rows of height bars rise
marks.m3: the two families are named at the left of the rows
marks.m4: a question mark rises beside the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is an example from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It gives the heights of two families in centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>{{NAME_8}}'s family has six members, and {{NAME_1}}'s family has five.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which single number describes each family best?

beats.on_screen: the two rows of bars stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of five bars sorts from shortest to tallest; the bar in the middle lights up and the word median appears above it

marks.g1: a single bar stands for the whole row, the mean
marks.g2: the row of five bars sorts from shortest to tallest
marks.g3: the bar in the middle lights up with the word median

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>The mean is one number that can stand for a group.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Here is another, found by sorting the heights from shortest to tallest.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The number in the middle of the sorted list is called the median.

marks.given: the heading heights in centimetres is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_8}}'s family has these heights in centimetres.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>One hundred and sixty nine, one hundred and seventy three, and one hundred and fifty five.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Then one hundred and sixty five, one hundred and sixty, and one hundred and sixty four.
<bookmark mark='g4'/>{{NAME_1}}'s family has these heights in centimetres.
<bookmark mark='g5'/>One hundred and seventy, one hundred and seventy three, and one hundred and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='g6'/>Then one hundred and eighteen, and one hundred and seventy five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mean and the median of each family, and which number represents the family better

marks.find: the words mean, median and represents are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the mean and the median of each family, and see which fits better.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, mean = total ÷ number of members: {{NAME_8}} 986 ÷ 6 ≈ 164.33 cm; {{NAME_1}} 801 ÷ 5 = 160.2 cm

marks.s1: the rule mean = total ÷ number of members is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, find the mean of each family.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>{{NAME_8}}'s heights add up to nine hundred and eighty six.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>Divided by six, the mean is about one hundred and sixty four point three three.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>{{NAME_1}}'s heights add up to eight hundred and one.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>Divided by five, the mean is one hundred and sixty point two.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, median of {{NAME_1}}'s family: sorted 118, 165, 170, 173, 175; five values, so the middle one is 170 cm

marks.d1: {{NAME_1}}'s five heights are sorted from shortest to tallest
marks.d2: the sorted row is shown with the shortest height first
marks.d3: the third height, 170, is circled with two on each side

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, find the median of {{NAME_1}}'s family.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Sorted, the heights run from one hundred and eighteen to one hundred and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>There are five heights, so the middle one has two on each side.
The median is one hundred and seventy centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, median of {{NAME_8}}'s family: sorted 155, 160, 164, 165, 169, 173; six values, so (164 + 165) ÷ 2 = 164.5 cm

marks.e1: {{NAME_8}}'s six heights are sorted from shortest to tallest
marks.e2: the third and fourth heights, 164 and 165, are circled
marks.e3: a mark halfway between them reads 164.5

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>Step three, find the median of {{NAME_8}}'s family.
Sorted, the heights run from one hundred and fifty five to one hundred and seventy three.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>There are six heights, so two of them share the middle.
<bookmark mark='e3'/>The median is halfway between one hundred and sixty four and one hundred and sixty five.
That is one hundred and sixty four point five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, compare mean and median: {{NAME_8}} 164.33 and 164.5 are close; {{NAME_1}} 160.2 and 170 are far apart

marks.f1: the mean and the median of each family sit side by side
marks.f2: {{NAME_8}}'s two numbers are marked close together
marks.f3: {{NAME_1}}'s two numbers are marked far apart

narration: <bookmark mark='f1'/>Step four, compare the mean and the median of each family.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>For {{NAME_8}}'s family they are close, so either number works.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>For {{NAME_1}}'s family they are far apart, one hundred and sixty point two and one hundred and seventy.

beats.on_screen: Answer: {{NAME_8}}: mean ≈ 164.33 cm, median 164.5 cm; {{NAME_1}}: mean 160.2 cm, median 170 cm; the median represents the family better
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The median represents {{NAME_1}}'s family better.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble shows a line at the mean 160.2 across {{NAME_1}}'s five bars; four bars stand above the line and one lies below it

marks.doubt: the bubble with the mean line appears
marks.fix: the line is drawn across {{NAME_1}}'s family and four bars stand above it
marks.idea: the short bar of 118 lights up as the one pulling the mean down

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mean is the best number for every family, because it uses every height.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>In {{NAME_1}}'s family, four of the five members are taller than the mean.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>One short member pulls the mean down, and the median stays in the middle.
